fix.summary:
#131 round 5 (final round) is done in /tmp/wt-131. It is still one commit on aab1f210: 3374439f, amended from 808ac7ae with --cleanup=verbatim. Not pushed and not rebased.

Item 1 (verify B, the regression). The selector error no longer reads the cache to decide whether a catalog is registered. It now asks the registered sources: the effective list, which includes the built-in default. The new code is extension_install._catalog_selector_problem, plus extension_catalog.location_matches_selector and cached_copy. An absolute selector is now compared by the file it names, so a symlinked spelling, or /tmp vs /private/tmp, selects the stored catalog. After discover install <name> --catalog <sel> finds nothing:
- If the selector names a registered catalog the cache has no copy of, the message says so and says to run discover --refresh. That covers source add before any refresh, an https catalog an offline refresh skipped, and a relative registration cached before registeredAs.
- If it picks only catalogs whose last refresh failed, the message names the catalog with its recorded error and says to refresh.
- Only a selector that names no registered catalog says 'matches no registered catalog'. When some registered catalog has no fetched copy yet, the message adds that its name is not known until a refresh.
- With no --catalog, the plain hint is unchanged.
On 808ac7ae all five shapes printed the false message, and a failed refresh got the generic hint. Rows were red before and are green after: 10 rows fail on 808ac7ae sources.

Item 2 (verify NBs):
- scp rewrite: the guide, its bundled copy, ADR-0255 and the CHANGELOG now say git+ssh://git@host/path.
- 'name @ <URL ending in .git>' (argv becomes 'git+name @ ...'): not fixed. It is older than this change, aab1f210 does the same to a typed target, and it reads nothing from the cwd. It is not trivial: the same string feeds the argv (_normalize_git_spec), the git pin identity (_git_repo_identity) and the recorded source key (_target_source_key). The docs now state it and advise writing the git URL without the name. Follow-up text is below.
- Space before extras: aligned with pip. split_path_extras now right-strips the path part, as pip 26.2.1's strip_extras does. The argv carries '<abs>/x.whl[feature]', which uv also accepts.
- Broader claim: the round-4 summary said 'the staged copy keeps its extras now; on 751ec582 they were dropped'. That was broader than the code: 751ec582 already built f'{staged}{extras}', and only the literal-sibling collision lost the extras. The commit message and ADR section 9 already said 'in that case'. The correction is recorded in the message.
- Mutants: rows now pin 10 of verify's 12 survivors:
  - W09: a backslash in a bare archive name is refused.
  - W10: an upper-case .WHL suffix installs beside a local catalog and is refused from an https one.
  - W17: ACME.GIT is refused.
  - W22: the catalog diagnosis runs only for --catalog.
  - W11-W16: the six exception/spec lines, each fed an OSC 52 payload. W15 and W16 type the spec, because the cache loader drops a catalog entry that carries control characters.
  - W21 and W23 are equivalent. W21: http and git locations never form absolute paths, and an absolute *.git path is matched by its string. W23: build_index_catalog resolves relative_to itself; a row through a symlinked directory pins the outcome.

Item 3: the whole suite on aab1f210 fails only the sdist size cap, as expected (6,006,581 B). On a scratch cherry-pick onto 339f8735, tests/packaging_gate has 84 passed.

Docs updated: ADR-0255 (status line, section 2 (B), (C) and item 9, new section 10), the guide and its bundled copy (identical), the CHANGELOG, and the commit message (WHAT CHANGED, a new REVIEW ROUND 4 section, and a new 'EVIDENCE (review round 4) AND GATES' section).

blocking.title: A catalog source 'name @ <URL ending in .git>' still installs from the cwd with the pip backend, while ADR-0255, the guide, the CHANGELOG and the commit say it reads nothing from the cwd / does not install
blocking.detail: resolve_entry_target accepts 'acme-notes @ https://h.example.invalid/o/r.git' (form B, passed on unchanged). classify_target calls it git because it ends in .git, and _normalize_git_spec puts git+ in front of the whole string: 'git+acme-notes @ https://h.example.invalid/o/r.git'. uv 0.11.19 rejects that string with a parse error. pip 26.2.1 does not recognise it as a URL (it reads the scheme as 'git+acme-notes @ https', which is unknown), so it treats the string as a path relative to the cwd: it collapses the '//' and installs the directory 'git+acme-notes @ https:/h.example.invalid/o/r.git' if the cwd holds one. The same happens for 'name @ git+https://.../r.git' and for the forms with [extras]. This is pre-existing (aab1f210 behaves identically). But it breaks the #131 invariant on the #131 surface, and this round's docs claim the opposite. ADR-0255 section 2 (B) says it 'reads nothing from the cwd' and repeats that in section 10. The guide and its bundled copy say it 'does not install today'. The CHANGELOG says it 'does not install yet'. The commit message says it 'reads nothing from the cwd'. The brief said 'fix if trivial', and at the catalog layer it is trivial. It also matches the allowlist's own rule (refuse, never rewrite): in resolve_entry_target, refuse a 'name @ URL' direct reference that classify_target would route as git (the URL ends in .git, compared case-insensitively). Give the advice the docs already give (write git+https://host/o/r.git without the name) and add a row. The rewrite of typed targets (_normalize_git_spec, _git_repo_identity, _target_source_key) can stay a follow-up. If the main loop prefers not to fix it now, the four claims must at least be corrected and the follow-up re-prioritised. Exposure: pip and pipx installs only (a uv tool venv has no pip, so it uses uv, which fails safely), and POSIX only, since ':' is not allowed in Windows file names.

nonblocking.title: Item 1 residue: one narrow case still prints a false 'the catalog cache has no copy recorded for it'
nonblocking.detail: Setup: a hand-edited relative registration {spec: 'catalog.json'}, refreshed from its own directory, so the cache holds it with registeredAs. From another directory, '--catalog ./catalog.json' (or that directory's absolute catalog.json path) gets 'names the registered catalog 'catalog.json', but the catalog cache has no copy recorded for it'. That is false: cached_copy(catalogs, 'catalog.json') returns the copy. The cause is that location_matches_selector anchors the relative spec at the CURRENT cwd, while the cached copy was anchored at the refresh cwd. Following the advice from that directory replaces the good copy with an error row. 808ac7ae printed 'matches no registered catalog' here, which was also false, so this is not a regression. Suggested fix: in the 'named' branch, when cached_copy(named[0]) exists, say that its copy was read from <cached location> and that '--catalog catalog.json' selects it.
nonblocking.evidence: live5b-head.txt R1: from elsewhere, '--catalog catalog.json' resolves and installs (consent n), but '--catalog ./catalog.json' and '--catalog <W>/elsewhere/catalog.json' get the 'no copy recorded' message. live5b-r4-808ac7ae.txt: 'matches no registered catalog' for both.

nonblocking.title: The not-fetched message's reasons leave out the offline-skip case, and its '--refresh' advice cannot work under AELIX_OFFLINE=1
nonblocking.detail: The fix summary and ADR item 9 say this message covers 'an https catalog an offline refresh skipped'. The text only offers two reasons: 'not fetched since it was registered' or 'cache written before registeredAs'. After an offline refresh rewrote the cache without a catalog that had been fetched before, neither reason is true. With AELIX_OFFLINE=1 set, the advice 'Fetch it with: aelix extension discover --refresh' skips the https catalog or the built-in default again, so the user loops. The same goes for the 'N registered catalog(s) have no fetched copy ... run refresh first' note: an air-gapped user whose default is not suppressed sees it on every unknown selector.
nonblocking.evidence: live-head.txt B7: the https catalog was fetched and failed in B6, then 'discover --refresh --offline' dropped it, then: '... has not been fetched since it was registered ...'. N3: AELIX_OFFLINE=1 with --catalog set to the default URL gives the same message, and the advice is a plain --refresh.

findings.title: Uppercase FILE:/// scheme is accepted, then uv installs it from the cwd (cat 1, P1)
findings.detail: The resolver lowercases the scheme to decide that the source is an absolute file URL, but passes the original string through unchanged. uv does not treat uppercase 'FILE:' as a URL scheme. It reads the whole string as a relative path and opens <cwd>/FILE:/<abs path>. The cwd-shadow guard checks the whole 'name @ URL' string, so it misses this. Real CLI, real uv backend, default verification: exit 0, and the installed wheel is the cwd decoy.

findings.title: Resolved path containing '#', '[]' or a trailing space is reinterpreted by uv, so a different directory is installed than the one printed (cat 1/2, P1 per Codex)
findings.detail: The catalog says {"name":"probe","source":"./link"}. cat/link is a symlink to cat/trusted#release, cat/trusted[] or 'cat/trusted ' (each holding version 1.0). cat/trusted is a symlink to a decoy directory holding version 9.0. aelix resolves ./link to the intended path, prints it and hands it to uv. uv then treats '#release' as a URL fragment, strips the empty extras '[]' and strips the trailing whitespace, so it opens cat/trusted, which is the decoy. The bracket regex at extension_catalog.py:1397 misses empty []. The path acceptance guard at extension_catalog.py:1473 does not model how the backend reinterprets paths. Caveat from the orchestrator, not from Codex: the decoy is a directory named 'cwd/decoy' in the fixture, not the process cwd, and both symlinks sit in the catalog directory. So this shows that the printed path differs from the installed path, which breaks the docs' claim that the resolved path is what gets installed. It does not show a pure cwd read.

findings.title: The refusal message for 'file:/abs' (single slash) wrongly says the installer would read it from the cwd (cat 2)
findings.detail: Refusing the single-slash spelling matches ADR-0255's file:/// requirement. The message given, however, claims that the source is not absolute and that the installer would read it from the current directory. That is false: the parent commit's CLI and the raw uv backend both install the named absolute catalog wheel. The message should say the spelling is unsupported. Separately, the docs' guarantee that the resolved path is what gets installed is contradicted by the two findings above.

findings.title: A versioned requirement 'local-ext==1.0' is refused when a file with that exact name sits beside the catalog (cat 3, P2; also contradicts ADR-0255 line 155)
findings.detail: The collision guard at extension_catalog.py:1506 compares the entire versioned requirement with the names of files next to the catalog, so an unrelated file named 'local-ext==1.0' blocks the index install. The parent commit installed it fine. ADR-0255 line 155 says a version specifier 'is not checked' for neighbouring-file ambiguity, and this contradicts it. Codex also reproduced the refusal of 'local-ext==1.0; python_version >= "3.11"' (parent exit 0, current exit 2), but notes that this one is intended by the ADR.
